title: Old Boy
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Shinichi Goto is kidnapped and held for ten years in a private prison with only a television for company, then released without explanation. He trains body and mind during captivity and, once free, hunts for the person who imprisoned him and the reason why, drawn into a game his captor has not finished playing. A seinen crime noir told mostly through investigation, dialogue and mind games.
life_message: A man stripped of his life endures by discipline of mind, but the pursuit of revenge binds hunter and hunted together.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: A childhood humiliation is answered by a decade-long personal revenge; Goto seeks his own reckoning, not the courts.

Order vs freedom.evidence: Goto acts alone outside law and institutions after release.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Personal grudges rather than family or community loyalties drive events.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: The captor commands a private prison and hired staff (MU Rich Character/s); no clear stance on rank.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Modern urban noir; reason and investigation, no religion.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Survival, endurance and physical training dominate Goto's life.

folkways.japan: The story draws on Japanese anxieties about losing face and childhood school relationships, with a sixth-grade class and its teacher central to the backstory.

delivery.evidence: ANN calls the storytelling understated and driven by dialogue and reasoning; Wikipedia summary shows themes carried by the mystery plot.
delivery.note: The story leaves readers to draw conclusions about revenge from what happens to Goto and Kakinuma rather than stating a lesson.

winners_losers: The mystery centers on Goto's struggle, but the revenge game damages both men; no side's worldview is presented as fully vindicated.
